claims.statement: Starting a proposal (POST /proposals) is refused with 404 if the org is unreadable, 403 unless the caller may run it (admins and stewards), and 409 unless the funder is in the org's latest saved Funder Match run; on success new_work creates work at stage 1 with requirements derived from the saved match detail, earlier_phase from the relationship criterion, a template pre-filled from the funder's newest proposal_template document, and a default style.

Step 1 requirements come from gates.build: 12A, 80G and audited accounts, plus CSR Form 1 for Section 135 funders (the only hard requirement), plus non-hard 'funder's own bar' items; steps.exit_check(1) blocks leaving until every requirement is answered yes/will_have/no and no hard requirement is answered no.

steps.exit_check is the single source of what stops a step, shared by POST /advance (409 with a missing list), the agent's advance_step and the screen's to_continue line; step 2 needs a form or usual order, a style, a file or funder reader started and none running, step 3 needs text in Context (A2) and Problem (A3), step 4 has no exit requirement, and step 5 is the last step.

Agent tools are gated by step in code (add_facts and read_files from step 2; ask_user, write_section and suggest_edit from step 3) via steps.too_early, and every writing tool first calls require_edit so a read-only member's run is refused.

readers.read is launched by code: under the proposal row lock (repo.save) it marks every pending reader running (each ticked file and the funder side, whenever not yet done), refusing with Busy if a non-stale reader of the same kind is running (stale after 30 minutes); readers then run in parallel behind a semaphore sized from max_parallel_research, each with its own sources (one document, or none for the funder reader), one failure never stops the others, and outcomes are written to work.readers via work.apply.

work.apply is the only way proposals.work changes: it checks every path and value first (nothing half-applied), enforces per-section rev (missing rev is BadChange, mismatched rev is StaleSection carrying the current section and who last changed it), logs each change with who, how and values, bumps each touched section's rev by one, and recomputes the summary.

The REST save path maps refusals to statuses: 403 for a reader, 422 for a source id that is not the org's own file, 400 for BadChange, 409 with missing for an advance not yet allowed, and 409 with message/section/current/changed_by for a stale section; repo.save takes the row FOR UPDATE and writes work and summary back.

Stage moves over PATCH may only go backwards; forward movement is only through advance (POST /advance or advance_step), which must pass exit_check, and an advance to the same or a lower step is refused.

Agent write_section refuses, in order, non-editors, early steps, unknown sections, empty or over-12,000-character text, sections out of DEPENDS_ON order (unless the part is open on screen, which never exempts the Summary), and any paragraph whose numbers, amounts, places or partner names are not in a live fact cited in that paragraph; only text that traces is then graded and saved at the section's next rev, and a stale rev is refused.

A person's own typing over REST is not refused by the trace check; work.apply instead derives untraced claims after saving (shown on screen and listed under Fix first), and _after_typing clears Done, needs_rewrite and the stale grade; score, needs_rewrite, missing, untraced and used_in cannot be set by a person, and grading on Done runs only for a current rev and never blocks a save.

ask_user questions are gated by questions.may_ask: only from step 3, only about the part on screen during steps 3 and 4 (step 5 has no on-screen restriction), one open question per person, one person per gap, and only for a warranted reason (missing, disagree, org_call); replies become confirmed you_said facts, and a later reply parks the question.

Correcting a fact over PATCH expands into a new fact plus the old one marked corrected, and review.follow rewrites sentences citing the old fact word for word only if no untraced claim is added, marks parts it cannot fix needs_rewrite, and returns derived facts to proposed.

readiness.summary, recomputed on every save, splits the review into Fix first (blocks ready) and Worth checking; ready is true only when Fix first is empty, and it does not gate the Word download. The same summary carries the open stage, to_continue and furthest used by the step bar.

POST /polish refuses with 409 if nothing is written, 502 if the model call fails, and 409 with a list of differences if any figure, place, name, gap or year changed; only a clean result is saved, code-only via polish, as work.polished with the section revs it was made from, and assemble.final uses smoothed text only for parts whose rev still matches.

POST /versions refuses with 503 when storage is off, 409 when nothing is written and 502 when the upload fails; otherwise it builds a .docx (gaps highlighted, source marks stripped), uploads it to the org Doc Vault as v<n>.docx, inserts a private AI-written proposal_draft document, and appends a numbered version with a facts snapshot via the code-only versions path, which refuses concurrent saves claiming the same number.

Each editor has a private chat thread per proposal with id proposal-<id>-<user id>; proposal_chat_access returns 404 for someone else's thread or unreadable org and 403 for a read-only member, the server sets the run's proposal id from the thread, GET /messages returns an empty list before the thread is opened, and teammates' changes reach the agent only through work.log.

On every model call ProposalContext re-reads the proposal and injects a cached 'This proposal' block and a fresh 'Right now' block including the step and part on screen, so a save between tool calls is seen by the next.

The screen's part editor debounces saves by 1.5 s, sends the section rev it last saw, and on a 409 stale response shows the other writer's current text while keeping the person's own text to copy from; ProposalShell polls every 5 s while readers run.

Feature availability in the Ask workspace is a front-end switch: COMING_SOON in features/ask/lib/comingSoon.ts is currently an empty set, so both Proposals and RFP Watch are enabled; the same set drives the sidebar items' soon flags and the separate main-area choice between ComingSoonView and ProposalsView / RfpWatchView, so each feature can be switched off independently by adding its name back.

Funder Match's proposal UI follows the same switch: with proposals out of COMING_SOON the card shows ProposalAction (Start a proposal, Continue/View proposal, Start another, or a Proposals (n) list link, with start buttons only when mayStart) and the view shows a Proposal filter (any / has / none); when in COMING_SOON the card shows a disabled button with a Coming soon tag and the filter is omitted.

Proposals are stored server-side in the proposals table (migration 0009) via repositories/proposals.py with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and routes/proposals.py; browser localStorage (sangam.proposals.v1) is only a leftover from the earlier browser-only store, checked by hadBrowserProposals.

RFP Watch calls are not linked to proposals in code: a CallCard offers Save, Not for us, Ask about this call (opens a new Ask chat seeded with a question via newChat) and a link out, while RfpWatchView's onFunderMatch merely switches to Funder Match, where Start a proposal lives; the rfp-watch views and backend proposals package contain no reference to each other.

Public research (secondary research) exists only when public tools and a Tavily search key are configured; it is the only reader with web access, its task is built from the registry's public rows and the match (never a file or the fact list), and a PublicGuard refuses searches naming the organisation and records the text of pages read. Its facts must pass facts.off_page: web origin only, sections A2, A3, A4, A14 or F1, a topic, a stated year, not Wikipedia, and an exact quote from a page read in that run containing every number of the value; they are stamped found_by public.

ProposalShell polls the proposal every 5 s while any reader (file or public) is running or, for an editor at step 2 or later, while the chat is mid-turn; its Reading your files card lists each ticked file and the funder's side with status, per-reader fact counts (using found_by to separate public research from the funder's web facts) and a Try again button for failures, and leaves public research to the step 3 Secondary research card.

The proposal has five steps in work.stage (Can you apply, Your documents and style, Make a case, Make a plan, Before you send it), named by steps.STAGES and mirrored in the front-end steps.ts; migration 0050 added Make a case as step 3 by adding 1 to work.stage and the stored summary.stage of every proposal already at step 3 or later, and rubric.stage_of puts the case tab on step 3 and every other tab on step 4.

A forward click can jump several steps: POST /advance?to=n runs steps.blocking, which requires exit_check to be empty for every step passed on the way, steps.furthest gives the last reachable step (the screen disables later buttons), and the agent's advance_step moves exactly one step; step buttons go back with PATCH stage and forward with advance.

Reading files and public research take separate locks: readers.pending looks only at running readers of the same kind (public or not), so a running search never holds up reading files and the reverse, and exit_check(2) ignores the public reader so a search alone does not count as reading the files.

Secondary research is started from the step 3 card by POST /proposals/{id}/research, which returns 202 and runs readers.search in a background task (a supervisor launching one researcher per angle, plus a separate brief written with Anthropic's web search and fetch, whose failure never fails the search); it refuses 409 before step 2 or while a search is running and 503 without a search key, and the run's status, researcher lines and brief are written to work.readers.public.

Research deeper and reset are code-checked: GET /research/angles needs Context (A2) and Problem (A3) marked done (409 otherwise), has the utility model turn the case into up to eight angles and drops any naming the org, funder, a partner or a person (502 on model failure); DELETE /research runs research.reset with via=reset, refuses 409 while a search runs or when nothing exists, and removes readers.public, research_asks and every public fact that no part cites, no fact derives from and no correction replaced.

repo.save first queues on a per-proposal in-process asyncio.Lock and only then opens a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, because many parallel researchers waiting on the row lock had held every pooled connection; the queue is per process, and the row lock still serialises the actual write.

DELETE /proposals/{id} (editors only, 204) deletes the row and the private proposal_draft documents under that proposal's own org-vault folder in one transaction, then removes their files; if storage cannot delete a file the transaction rolls back and the route answers 502 so the proposal is kept, and a draft another row still references is left; migration 0052 grants the delete.

POST /versions with shape form fills the funder's own form: it refuses 409 when step 2 chose no form, 422 when the form cannot be read and 502 on model failure; form.read stores the outline once under the code-only template.outline path, fill.fill answers every prose and field heading in one call, and fill.resolve keeps an answer only if it adds no figure, place or name and fits the limit, otherwise marking [Add: ...] or, for fields, tables and annexes, [You fill: ...]; the version entry carries shape form and a report.
